title: WHAT’S NEW IN MY DATA? NOVELTY EXPLORATION VIA CONTRASTIVE GENERATION
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the model's generation of toxic language and hate speech aimed at various minority groups as a way to discover novel properties in fine-tuning datasets. Within this context, it measured the generation of toxic text targeting Muslims and Jewish people (among other groups) and the ability of an evaluator model to correctly classify the target group of the generated hate speech.
findings: The study found that Contrastive Generative Exploration (CGE) could successfully identify and generate novel toxic text that had been introduced during fine-tuning. The evaluator model (LLaMA 3) was able to correctly classify the target groups of the generated toxic text—which included Muslims and Jewish people—with 95.5% accuracy. However, specific bias metrics or generation rates isolated solely for the religious groups were not independently reported, as they were part of a broader evaluation of 10 minority groups.
